title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted recordings without permission or licensing agreements. The system could generate music similar to specific tracks, showing that copyrighted works were in its training data. This is a model deployment failure: the system was built and released using material its creators did not have the right to use, a condition that should have been verified before launch.

Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group later reached settlements with Udio that included licensing agreements and plans for a new platform trained only on authorized music. Sony Music filed separate lawsuits alleging Udio used over 30,000 recordings without authorization, and a court declined to dismiss a class action by independent artists. It is not established whether Udio intentionally targeted specific works, whether the company understood the legal requirements before launch, or what the final outcomes of ongoing litigation will be.

summary:
Universal Music Group has reached a settlement with AI music startup Udio, ending a lawsuit that accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. The case alleged that Udio used famous tracks like The Temptations' "My Girl" to create similar melodies without permission or compensation. Under the new licensing agreements, Udio will launch a platform next year trained only on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to customize, stream, and share songs they create. Artists can opt into the platform and will receive compensation for their work, though specific details remain undisclosed.

This settlement represents Udio's first major licensing deal with a record label and reflects ongoing tension between the music industry and AI companies over copyright protection. Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, allows users to generate original music from text prompts. The company has attracted millions of users since launching and counts musician will.i.am and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz among its backers. UMG also announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
